# Scope: com.desertstormfront.ui.{SpriteBatch, GlBuffer, FrameBuffer, ClipRect} (30 methods +
# 22 fields) - the immediate-mode renderer front end. Evidence per symbol:
# ClipRect: the four ints are the clip bounds. SpriteBatch's clipping code fixes the order: a()/c()
#   are the x range (rejected when x > c() and clamped when x < a()), b()/d() the y range ->
# SpriteBatch: a=BatchRenderer (the owner that owns the vertex buffers), b=clipRect, c=the current
#   ARGB colour, and the two shorts d/e are that colour split for the shader: d = (c & 0xFF00) |
#   (c >> 16 & 0xFF) = the red/green byte pair, e = (c >> 16 & 0xFF00) | (c & 0xFF) = blue/alpha
#   -> colorRG / colorBA. a(int) is the colour setter (it caches the packed shorts) -> setColor ;
#   a(ClipRect) -> setClipRect. The five a(...) draw overloads all funnel into the short one:
#   (x, y, width, height, u, v, uvWidth, uvHeight, colour), with float/int/shape variants simply
#   rounding or widening first - so all of them become draw(...). Verified against the shared body,
#   which writes two triangles using (u,v)..(u+uw, v+vh).
# GlBuffer: a=GL target (GL_ARRAY_BUFFER / GL_ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER), b=size in bytes,
#   c=the direct NIO buffer, d=the GL name -> target/sizeBytes/data/bufferId. The private
#   a(target, size, buffer, usage) creates and uploads -> upload ; c() binds -> bind ;
#   d() re-uploads the whole buffer (glBufferSubData from 0) -> uploadAll ;
#   a(offset, length) -> uploadRange ; e() unbinds -> unbind ; f() deletes the GL name -> dispose ;
#   a()/b() are the size/data accessors -> getSize/getData.
# FrameBuffer: d=target, e=the GL framebuffer name, f/g=width/height, h=the attached GlTexture,
#   a is the currently bound FrameBuffer (used to restore on unbind), b the default framebuffer name
#   f() checks glCheckFramebufferStatus and logs a readable error -> checkStatus ;
#   a()/b() -> getWidth/getHeight ; c() binds and sets the viewport -> bind ;
#   d()/a(boolean) restore the previous (or default) framebuffer -> unbind(boolean toDefault) ;
#   e() deletes the renderbuffer and framebuffer -> dispose.
# No member here is reached by name (no reflection, no persistence): these are pure GL wrappers.
